headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Firecrawl’s broad egress plus Replit Agent’s writable Repl workspace can expose secrets and overwrite shared state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through scrape/crawl outputs, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Firecrawl output is copied into the workspace or otherwise fed to the agent. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is written into a Replit workspace file and then opened by Replit Agent as prompt context, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared file or copy-paste workflow, attacker-controlled web text can influence agent behavior.
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs in a separate review file and never feed raw HTML/markdown directly to the agent.
Add a manual sanitization step that strips instructions before reuse.
Use a read-only staging directory for scraped content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to scraped artifacts before agent consumption.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, and has broad network egress. Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration, with writable Repl files and broad egress. If they share a workspace or secrets are copied between them, sensitive data can leave the environment through either agent’s outbound requests.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes API keys or screenshots that are then stored in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can read them.
IF either agent forwards workspace contents to external APIs, secrets and source code can be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Store secrets only in dedicated secret managers, not workspace files.
Disable copying Firecrawl outputs into the Repl unless redacted.
Review outbound requests before running either agent on sensitive data.
Use separate accounts/projects for scraping and coding.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret-scanning gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support and broad egress; Replit Agent can execute shell, modify git state, and write the filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The profiles document overlapping mutable surfaces, so the conflict is direct.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, simultaneous edits can overwrite each other.
IF Replit Agent commits while Firecrawl writes generated artifacts into the same tree, git history can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file.
Have only one agent modify git state.
Run Firecrawl in read-only mode when possible.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking around shared repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped content and extracted data that Replit Agent could treat as input for coding or deployment tasks. Replit Agent has shell and deployment authority, so an unverified Firecrawl result can cascade into incorrect code changes or operational actions. The pair does not prove automatic trust, but the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as authoritative input for Replit Agent without verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF Replit Agent deploys or edits code based on scraped data, errors can propagate into production artifacts.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on scraped outputs.
Keep source citations alongside extracted facts.
Use a validation script before deployment.
Limit Replit Agent to draft-only changes for Firecrawl-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Firecrawl outputs before consumption.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches screenshots, web content, structured data, and API keys; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. If regulated or personal data is scraped into a Repl workspace, Replit’s cloud-hosted processing and logging/retention practices may differ from the source environment. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF EU personal data or PHI is copied from Firecrawl into a Replit workspace, residency and retention obligations may change.
IF the operator lacks a DPA or approved processing basis for Replit-hosted handling, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent unless approved.
Redact personal data before transfer between agents.
Check vendor DPAs and retention settings before use.
Keep a data-class inventory for scraped artifacts.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant environment.
